subject: science
domain: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

items.answer: Maintaining stable internal conditions in the body

items.prompt: What does the body do when it gets too hot?

steps: Sweating cools the body back toward normal.

items.prompt: What does the body do when it gets too cold?

steps: Shivering generates heat to warm the body.

items.prompt: What hormone lowers blood sugar after a meal?

steps: Insulin lowers blood sugar back to normal.

items.prompt: Do feedback mechanisms help keep conditions stable?
Sweating when hot is an example of what?

steps: Sweating is a feedback response to cool down.

items.prompt: In negative feedback, a change is responded to in order to do what?
items.answer: Reverse it and return to normal

steps: Negative feedback reverses the change toward the set point.

items.prompt: Name one internal condition the body keeps stable.

steps: Temperature and blood sugar are kept stable.

items.prompt: Does homeostasis work even when outside conditions change?

steps: Homeostasis keeps inside stable despite outside changes.

items.answer: The normal level a condition is kept near

steps: The set point is the target level for a condition.

items.answer: When too hot, the body sweats to cool back to its normal temperature

steps: Sweating reverses the rise in temperature.

items.prompt: Describe an investigation to show feedback controls body temperature.
items.answer: Measure temperature during exercise and rest to see it rise then return to normal

steps: The return to normal shows feedback at work.

items.prompt: Why does the body release insulin after eating?
items.answer: To lower the raised blood sugar back to normal

steps: Insulin brings blood sugar back to the set point.

items.prompt: How does negative feedback keep temperature near normal?
items.answer: A rise triggers cooling and a fall triggers warming, both returning it to normal

steps: Opposite responses push temperature back to the set point.

items.prompt: Why is shivering a feedback response?
items.answer: It generates heat to warm a too-cold body back to normal

steps: Shivering reverses a drop in temperature.
